items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: He hired Ben Webster as the saxophone player

ctx.x: So, there wasn't any horns in the jungle, really, you know? But he said, "Okay, you can get some violins." So, he started scrambling around town, trying to find some black violin players. So, luckily somebody told him, said, "That little Marshal Royal boy can play violins." So, they found me down at the Apex, which was next door to the Dunbar Hotel, the Somerville Hotel at that time, where Duke was staying, where everybody of note in -- that was black stayed when they came to town, was that one hotel.

So, he came down and told me that he would like to have me play the violin on Check and Double Check. // So, we went out there and he wrote out some violin parts and things and we played the violin parts. They probably cut it out. I don't remember whether they cut the violin parts out of the score or whether it was actually in the picture or not. But that was my introduction to Duke Ellington as a violin player. So, I actually was supposed to have gone back with the Ellington band later on around the mid-'30s as…
Well, had joining while he was here. Did he talk to you about (inaudible)?
